records.title: Limonin Targets USP7 to Remodel the Gastric Epithelial Barrier via Activating Rap1A/Rac1 Signaling.
records.abstract: Acute gastric mucosal injury impairs gastrointestinal homeostasis with limited clinical repair strategies. As a natural triterpenoid, limonin exerts gastric mucosal protection, while its precise target and mechanism remain elusive. We verified that limonin alleviated ethanol-induced gastric damage, suppressed inflammation and apoptosis, and promoted epithelial repair in rat models and GES-1 cells. Mechanistically, limonin directly binds USP7 at MET410 to strengthen the USP7-Rap1A interaction. It enhances USP7-mediated K31 deubiquitination to block K48-linked Rap1A proteasomal degradation, activating the Rap1A/Rac1 cascade. This signaling remodels epithelial tight junctions and cytoskeletons. Genetic and pharmacological USP7 inhibition abolished limonin's protection, which was further validated in iPSC-derived gastric organoids. This study identifies a novel USP7-Rap1A axis underlying limonin's gastroprotective effects.

records.title: Promotion of the Proliferation and Migration of Breast Cancer Cells by the Micro Ribonucleic Acid miR-425-5p via Dihydropyrimidinase-Like 2.
records.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most common malignant tumor in women. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a class of noncoding single-stranded RNA molecules that are closely related to the development, progression, and metastasis of BC. The miRNA miR-425-5p is upregulated in a variety of cancers and can promote cancer progression. This study aimed to investigate the role of miR-425-5p in BC and its molecular mechanism. The expression of miR-425-5p in BC was analyzed using the Cancer Genome Atlas database and two Gene Expression Omnibus validation cohorts. Expression of miR-425-5p in paired BC and adjacent nontumor tissues from four patients with invasive ductal carcinoma and in normal breast epithelial and BC cell lines. Expression of miR-425-5p in BC tissues and cell lines was detected via quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Protein expression was detected using a Western blot. Cell growth and proliferation were assessed via a 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay. A transwell assay was used to detect the migration ability of BC cells. The effects of miR-425-5p and DPYSL2 were verified using patient-derived BC organoids established from the four tumor samples, as well as xenograft experiments in female nude mice randomly divided into three groups (five or eight mice per group). The experimental results showed that miR-425-5p expression levels were higher in tumor tissue than in normal tissue. The RT-qPCR results showed high expression of miR-425-5p in clinical samples and BC cell lines; miR-425-5p promoted the growth and migration of BC cells and targeted and degraded the DPYSL2 messenger RNA. The DPYSL2 protein content decreased upon miR-425-5p overexpression. The MTT and Transwell assay results indicated that miR-425-5p regulated BC progression via DPYSL2. Inhibition of miR-425-5p or overexpression of DPYSL2 inhibited BC growth in organoid and nude mouse xenograft experiments. In summary, miR-425-5p promoted BC development by targeting DPYSL2.

records.title: Characterization of Pulmonary Tropism, Expression Kinetics and Safety of the Novel Adeno-Associated Virus-LungM3 Vector.
records.abstract: This study investigated the lung-targeting characteristics, dose- and time-dependent effects, and safety of a novel engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector, AAV-LungM3. In vitro, mouse primary lung organoids were transduced with AAV-LungM3 at doses of 103, 104, and 105 vector genomes (vg)/cell, and transduction was evaluated by fluorescence detection. For in vivo validation, C57BL/6 mice received intratracheal injection of AAV-LungM3 at doses of 0.5 × 1011, 1.0 × 1011, and 2.0 × 1011 vg. Flow cytometry was performed to assess the dose-dependent transduction specificity and efficiency of AAV-LungM3 in type I alveolar epithelial cells (AT1 cells) and type II alveolar epithelial cells (AT2 cells). Using the favorable dose determined by the dose-response assay, the temporal changes in AT2 cell transduction specificity and efficiency were further monitored over a 4-week period. In addition, hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, detection of peripheral blood inflammatory factors, and analysis of plasma biochemical indicators were used to evaluate early-phase safety. In vitro transduction increased in a dose-dependent manner. In vivo assays revealed that the AT2 cell transduction specificity of AAV-LungM3 decreased gradually with increasing viral dose, whereas its transduction specificity for AT1 cells increased. Nevertheless, no significant differences in the transduction efficiency of AT1 cells and AT2 cells were observed among all dose groups. Longitudinal monitoring indicated that week 2 was the preferred time point for AAV-LungM3 transduction. In conclusion, under the tested conditions, AAV-LungM3 exhibited targeting specificity to AT2 cells and favorable in vivo expression with no observed toxic effects, serving as a potential delivery platform for pulmonary gene therapy.

records.title: Conditional Mutant MAPT Overexpression in Neural Organoids Elicits Robust Tau Accumulation and Pathological Transcriptomic Responses.
records.abstract: Modeling neurodegenerative conditions in neural organoids presents a potential complement to existing preclinical translation pipelines. Prior neural organoid models have generally relied on human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines containing disease-relevant alleles. However, this strategy limits temporal control over the initiation and progression of pathological events. In this study, we provide a proof-of-concept framework showing that neurodegenerative phenotypes can be triggered by inducible expression cassettes. We developed an iPSC line harboring doxycycline-inducible mutant MAPT, which encodes the microtubule-associated protein tau that is implicated in tauopathies. Induction of mutant MAPT via doxycycline treatment in differentiating neural organoids yielded accumulation of phosphorylated tau, which localized inside individual neuron somas within the cortical plate-like regions. Importantly, measured transcriptomic responses to tau overexpression bore key similarities to human clinical transcriptomic data. Taken together, we present an approach for controlling the initiation and progression of proteinopathy-like pathology in neural organoid systems.

records.title: Liquid-Suspendable Metabolic Sensors Allow Real-Time Oxygen Consumption Monitoring in Caco-2 and Colon Organoid-Based Gut-on-a-Chip Models.
records.abstract: The organ-on-a-chip field is a rapidly evolving area of expertise, combining enhanced physiological relevance with a wide range of functional readouts across diverse cellular models. One such readout is oxygen metabolism, which serves as a key indicator of mitochondrial function. In this study, we utilized metabolic sensors designed for real-time measurement of oxygen consumption, reflecting aerobic respiration, within a commercially available microfluidic platform. We demonstrated that time-resolved detection of oxygen consumption is feasible within the system's microliter-scale volumes and that chemically induced changes in cellular oxygen metabolism can be monitored in real time in two ready-to-use gut-on-a-chip models. In summary, this novel application of metabolic sensors enables direct evaluation of mitochondrial function in complex cellular environments by addressing key analytical challenges often encountered in organ-on-a-chip systems due to their limited size and structural complexity.

records.title: Targeting tankyrase scaffolding in the β-catenin destruction complex by PROTAC overcomes the limitation of catalytic inhibitors in colorectal cancer.
records.abstract: Aberrant WNT/β-catenin signaling drives tumorigenesis and metastasis in cancer. Although enzymatic inhibitors of tankyrase (TNKS) effectively block AXIN degradation and stabilize the β-catenin destruction complex (DC), they have demonstrated limited efficacy in various colorectal cancer (CRC) models. Here, we demonstrate that, unexpectedly, the induction of AXIN puncta represents a major barrier to achieving therapeutic efficacy. Mechanistically, catalytic inhibition of TNKS prevents TNKS turnover and drives its accumulation in the DC, wherein the scaffolding function of TNKS induces AXIN puncta formation, rigidifies the DC, and impedes β-catenin turnover. Chemically induced degradation of TNKS overcomes this limitation by stabilizing AXIN without puncta formation, providing a deeper suppression of the WNT/β-catenin pathway activity and the proliferation of CRC cells harboring dysfunctional APC mutations. Collectively, these findings provide an explanation for the unsatisfactory outcomes of drugging the WNT/β-catenin signaling pathway by TNKS inhibitors and highlight TNKS degradation as a promising approach to treat WNT/β-catenin-driven CRC.

records.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
records.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.

records.title: The Tenocyte from Atom to Cell: A Critical Multiscale Synthesis Linking Collagen Chemistry, Tissue Mechanics, Cell Mechanobiology and Mathematical Modelling.
records.abstract: The tenocyte builds, maintains, senses and degrades one of the most mechanically demanding extracellular matrices in vertebrates, yet the chemical, physical, biological and mathematical descriptions of this system have developed in largely separate literatures. This review examines the tenocyte-matrix unit as a single causal system spanning eight orders of magnitude in length, organised around five transitions: from collagen chemistry to molecular mechanics; from molecule to fibril and fascicle; from tissue loading to the cellular mechanical stimulus; from stimulus to transcription; and from cellular output back to matrix composition. At each transition, we weigh competing hypotheses, identify where evidence is decisive and where it remains correlative, and state the governing equations. We integrate advances from 2021-2026, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases of human tendons, the establishment of PIEZO1 as a causal regulator of tendon stiffness, and microstructurally derived constitutive models. We argue that tendon homeostasis is a closed-loop control problem, formalised as a mechanostat with an inverted-U dose-response, and that the recurrent pathologies of tendon-tendinopathy, ageing, diabetic stiffening and fibrotic healing are failures of this loop rather than of any single component. An open-source computational companion (tenocyte-virtual-cell) is introduced, and a prioritised research agenda closes the review.

records.title: Primary-Tumor Transcriptomic Signatures Associated with Circulating Tumor Cells Status in Breast Cancer: From CTC-Negative Remodeling to CTC-Associated Metastatic Programs.
records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) play a central role in metastasis by enabling tumor dissemination through the bloodstream. However, the molecular transition from CTC-negative (CTC-) to CTC-positive (CTC+) states and their associated systemic remodeling remain poorly understood. Methods: We performed a transcriptomic comparison between CTC+, CTC-, and healthy individuals using RNA-seq data and a bioinformatics pipeline. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, survival modeling, and drug perturbation prediction to delineate the molecular determinants of CTC emergence and persistence. Results: Primary tumors from CTC+ patients exhibited distinct transcriptomic profiles characterized by the upregulation of genes involved in PI3K-Akt signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and chromatin regulation (e.g., HDAC1, JUN, KLK10), alongside the downregulation of immune activation pathways, including complement, B-cell receptor (BCR), and T-cell receptor (TCR) signaling. Multi-gene survival models derived from upregulated (KLK10, MEOX2, IRS4, RND2) and downregulated (ALDH3A1, PPP2R2B, IGF1R) hub genes significantly stratified patient outcomes (HR = 1.74-2.44, p < 0.01). In contrast, primary tumors from CTC- patients displayed early systemic transcriptional alterations relative to healthy controls, with 1700+ DEGs linked to MAPK/ERK and receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) signaling pathways, suggesting pre-metastatic immune reprogramming even before CTC detection. Drug repurposing analysis identified Trichostatin A, BX-795, and Alvocidib as candidate compounds capable of reversing the CTC+ transcriptional signature. Conclusions: Rather than supporting a strictly binary view of CTC status, our findings are consistent with a transcriptional continuum of distinct yet partially overlapping primary-tumor transcriptional states associated with CTC- and CTC+ status, highlighting a molecular shift from immune suppression to epigenetic adaptation that facilitates hematogenous dissemination. The identified multi-gene prognostic panels and small-molecule candidates provide a foundation for CTC-targeted therapeutic strategies and early detection biomarkers in breast cancer.

records.title: Single-Cell Whole-Transcriptome Detection Expands the Observable RNA Space for AI Virtual-Cell Models.
records.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has supplied cell atlases and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled virtual-cell models with scalable, gene-level descriptions of cellular state. Yet prevalent poly(A)-based counting assays capture only part of the RNA landscape. Here, "single-cell whole-transcriptome detection" denotes sequencing-based efforts to detect a broader range of RNA biotypes than conventional poly(A)-based gene counting; no assay detects or quantifies every cellular RNA species without bias. We compare RNA-capture scope, transcript-structure resolution, temporal labeling, spatial context, and additional modalities as distinct measurement dimensions. From a biosensing perspective, analytical sensitivity, transcript coverage, throughput, and assay bias determine which signals are available to computational models. We then examine cell-state representations, regulatory networks, dynamics, perturbation prediction, and foundation models. Total-RNA assays reveal additional non-coding RNAs, long-read methods inform transcript structure, and temporal assays constrain RNA kinetics. Whether these signals improve prediction beyond conventional gene-count inputs requires matched, task-specific model comparisons. We distinguish molecular observability, statistical association, predictive performance, and causal validation, which requires appropriate interventions. We propose benchmarks controlling sequencing depth, cost, model architecture, and held-out samples while testing feature ablations, out-of-distribution performance, uncertainty calibration, and experimental outcomes. Together, high-throughput poly(A)-based profiling and broader RNA measurements provide complementary cellular breadth and regulatory depth.

records.title: Virtual cells: progress and challenges from mechanistic modeling to data-driven integration.
records.abstract: Virtual cells aim to represent cellular states computationally and predict responses to genetic, chemical, environmental, temporal, and spatial conditions. For comparative purposes, this review uses state encoding (E), state transition (T), and observation decoding (D) as a conceptual abstraction spanning explicit mechanistic models, data-driven foundation and perturbation models, multimodal systems, and spatial and multiscale simulation. We examine model boundaries, data foundations, resource disclosure, out-of-distribution evaluation, causal evidence, and experimental validation. Independent benchmarks show that parameter count and training-set size do not automatically yield robust out-of-distribution generalization, while transcriptomic representations alone do not capture the full functional state of a cell. Trustworthy virtual cells will require perturbation-responsive transitions, cross-modal alignment, continuous-time dynamics, mechanistic constraints, calibrated uncertainty, independent experimental validation, and, where appropriate, closed-loop experimental feedback.

records.title: Progress of metabolomics-centric multi-omics research in medicine.
records.abstract: Metabolomics reveals molecular changes at the metabolic level during biological processes. Recent advancements, particularly through integration with other omics and artificial intelligence (AI), are advancing metabolic data analysis and multi-omics interpretation. This review introduces a "metabolomics-centric" paradigm as a conceptual framework for multi-omics integration, positioning metabolic readouts as the functional anchor for interpreting genotype-phenotype relationships. It also chronicles the evolution and medical applications of integration technologies. Our discussion first traces the field's evolution from bulk to single-cell and spatial methodologies, next surveys integration strategies to uncover mechanistic insights, and finally examines how AI-driven multimodal data integration and AI-optimized metabolomics workflows tackle persistent biological and computational challenges. Looking forward, this review identifies the AI virtual cell as a pivotal future direction for metabolomics-based multi-omics integration, calling for increased attention to its development to simulate dynamic molecular phenotypic networks within a multi-omics context.

records.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation.
records.abstract: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis-including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication. This review systematically examines the intersection of BMP4 biology and AI across three core domains: (1) AI-driven drug discovery targeting BMP4 signaling pathways, (2) deep learning-based protein structure prediction and computational modeling of BMP4 and its receptor complexes, and (3) clinical AI applications for BMP4-associated diseases. A narrative review with systematic search elements was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, bioRxiv, and arXiv for English-language publications from 2020 to 2026, supplemented by targeted searches via Semantic Scholar. Included studies were categorized as BMP4-specific, BMP receptor/BMP-pathway-targeted, or transferable AI methodology not yet applied to BMP4. We find that AI has accelerated BMP4-related research along multiple axes, though with important caveats. AlphaFold3 and related tools have generated high-confidence predicted models of BMP4-receptor complex architecture, aspects of which were previously intractable to experimental structure determination; these predictions remain to be fully validated experimentally. ML-guided virtual screening has identified first-in-class BMP pathway (receptor) modulators for FOP, although BMP4-specific small-molecule modulators have not yet been identified computationally. Single-cell transcriptomics combined with machine learning have revealed BMP4's context-dependent roles in glioblastoma cell state transitions and cancer-associated fibroblast biology; and LASSO-Cox regression models incorporating BMP4 expression have shown promising prognostic value in pancreatic adenocarcinoma and gastric cancer, pending prospective validation. Significant gaps persist-most notably the absence of BMP4-specific de novo protein design efforts, the scarcity of large-scale training datasets for BMP4-targeted drug discovery, and the limited integration of multimodal AI approaches in BMP4 clinical research. The convergence of BMP4 biology and AI represents a fertile research Frontier. While foundational tools are now in place, realizing the full translational potential of AI-augmented BMP4 research will require coordinated efforts in data generation, model development, and rigorous experimental and clinical validation. We outline priority directions for the next 5 years (approximately 2026-2031).

records.title: LM2KM: feature extraction from pretrained protein and molecular language models combined with quantum mechanics (QM) features for K M predictions.
records.abstract: The Michaelis constant (K M) is a key parameter for characterizing enzyme-substrate interactions and plays an essential role in enzyme kinetics modeling and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) applications. However, experimental determination of K M is labor-intensive, and existing computational prediction approaches remain limited in accuracy and scalability. In this study, we systematically evaluated pretrained protein and molecule language models for K M prediction by integrating four protein language models (PLMs) and two molecule language models (MLMs) to encode enzyme sequences and substrate structures, respectively. Principal component analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce feature dimensionality, and a wide range of representation combinations were assessed. Our results indicated that protein representations derived from the last four layers of ProtT5 using approximately 70 features, combined with 20 CLS-based molecular features from MolFormer, provided a well-balanced and efficient representation for K M prediction. In addition, the incorporation of quantum mechanics (QM) descriptors consistently improved prediction performance across all tested configurations, with the model R 2 of 0.537. In summary, this work provides a flexible and extensible framework for large-scale K M prediction, with strong potential to facilitate enzyme pathway identification, drug and lead screening, and sequence-based protein design, supporting broader applications in enzyme kinetics-driven modeling and drug development.

records.title: AI-guided De Novo design of DHPS inhibitors.
records.abstract: Hypusine modification of eIF5A by Deoxyhypusine Synthase (DHPS) is essential for the replication of a broad range of viruses, making DHPS an attractive host-directed therapy (HDT) target for antiviral drug discovery. AI-based drug design methods spanning binding affinity prediction and de novo molecular generation are rapidly proliferating, yet systematic benchmarking of diverse algorithmic paradigms under identical conditions on a shared target, with experimental validation, remains scarce. Here, we present an integrated AI benchmarking pipeline targeting DHPS and evaluate the full process from computational prediction to experimental validation. We compared 13 MM-GBSA score estimation models and 10 de novo molecular generation methods under 5-seed repeated experiments. For the prediction task, we propose an Out-of-Fold stacking ensemble integrating gradient boosting, graph neural networks, and chemical language models, achieving the highest Spearman rank correlation of 0.861 among all compared models. For the generation task, we propose RL-Design, a reinforcement learning-based framework using the ensemble predictor as a scoring oracle. RL-Design achieved the highest hit rate of 92.02% and maintained drug-like physicochemical properties across generated molecules, outperforming all nine competing methods. Moreover, experimental dose-response assays confirmed inhibitory activity in all three predicted-active compounds, with two highly active compounds showing IC50 values of 31.2 and 49.1 µM. Predicted and experimental activity showed complete concordance across all six tested compounds, providing oracle-independent validation of the pipeline. This pipeline provides a reproducible framework for AI-guided, target-specific inhibitor design and demonstrates the feasibility of HDT-focused antiviral drug discovery through systematic AI benchmarking.Scientific contributionThis work proposes two methods for inhibitor discovery against DHPS, a host-directed antiviral target. A predictive model for MM-GBSA binding-score estimation and a generative model that designs candidate hit compounds both ranked first among previous prediction and generation models under identical benchmarking. The predicted activities were experimentally confirmed by dose-response enzymatic assays.

records.title: Simulating Directed Evolution In Silico with an Iterative, Physics-Based Workflow.
records.abstract: Directed evolution consistently delivers engineered enzymes that facilitate diverse biocatalytic transformations. Despite advances in automation and high-throughput workflows, our ability to rapidly engineer novel enzymes is limited by our inability to thoroughly sample the vast protein design space. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) methods have alleviated this challenge to some degree, due to their ability to propose mutations based on learned patterns from complex protein data sets. However, the hidden logic of these AI-based methods can complicate our ability to reveal and exploit fundamental details of these enzymes. To complement these hidden-logic models, we present a structure- and physics-based workflow that mimics directed evolution in silico. This Virtual Protein EngineeR (referred to as ViPER) aims to simulate directed evolution by leveraging computational modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, in silico mutagenesis, and structure-based property evaluation to iteratively engineer an enzyme toward a desired target. In this work, we present a retrospective analysis to demonstrate ViPER's ability to efficiently navigate the complex protein-protein interfaces associated with the oligomerization of a ketoreductase (KRED) enzyme. In addition to successfully predicting >70% of sites that are crucial for toggling the oligomerization of this KRED enzyme (after only five rounds), this dynamics-based methodology identifies a distal mutation that was incorporated during experiment-based directed evolution. This work provides a novel foundation for computationally driven directed evolution efforts, opening the opportunity to simultaneously pursue and evaluate multiple evolutionary routes through a physics-based lens.

records.title: Filling the massive AI drug discovery data gap.
Evaluating generative models for structure-based drug discovery from de novo design to lead optimization.
records.abstract: Advances in protein structure prediction have created opportunities for structure-based drug design, yet translating structural knowledge into actionable small-molecule ligands remains difficult. Existing benchmarks often use simplified datasets and computational surrogates that poorly capture the heterogeneity and constraints of real-world drug discovery. We introduce MolGenBench, a comprehensive benchmark for de novo molecular generation and hit-to-lead optimization built on a large, structurally diverse dataset. Evaluation of 17 leading methods reveals persistent limitations, including weak virtual-screening performance, limited coverage of target-specific bioactive space, frequent high-risk structural motifs, poor target awareness, and reduced generalization to unseen proteins. Although some models improve three-dimensional conformation generation, they still struggle to produce active molecules reliably. MolGenBench provides standardized data, metrics, and analyses that connect structural prediction with practical molecular design and guide the development of more effective structure-based generative models.

records.title: Satellite DNA: Intragenomic and Extracellular Dispersion.
records.abstract: Satellite DNA has traditionally been described as a chromosomal tandem-repeat fraction, mainly associated with the formation of constitutive heterochromatin. However, this description, although correct, does not fully capture interpretations that view satellite sequences as dynamic components of genome architecture, especially in response to stress and instability associated with pathological states such as cancer. In this article, satellite DNA is presented in its full biological dynamism, from chromosomal arrays to extracellular release, with a proposed intermediate extrachromosomal state. Rolling-circle-mediated replacement-repair offers a coherent molecular route capable of explaining not only the turnover of tandem arrays but also the extrachromosomal and extracellular phases. The demonstration of extracellular human alpha-satellite DNA in plasma strongly supports the concept that satellite DNA release is closely connected to the idea of a circulating indicator of cancer-associated genomic instability. This framework links satellite DNA evolution to liquid biopsy and suggests a broader role for repetitive DNA in translating genome dynamics into measurable disease signals.

records.title: Preliminary development and internal evaluation of a plasma SOX1 methylation-based model bladder cancer detection.
records.abstract: The evaluation of individuals with suspected bladder cancer (BCa) continues to rely on cystoscopy, while urine cytology demonstrates limited sensitivity. This single-center retrospective two-gate case-control study included 90 individuals (30 with BCa and 60 non-cancer controls). SOX1 methylation signals in plasma-derived DNA were quantified using quantitative methylation-specific PCR. Logistic regression was used to generate a SOX1-only model and a combined model incorporating SOX1 methylation, age, and sex. Model performance was described using apparent ROC-AUC, sensitivity, specificity and other operating characteristics at the Youden-derived cut-off, together with internal bootstrap, five-fold cross-validation, calibration, and exploratory decision-curve analysis (DCA). All resampling procedures used the same 90 participants; no independent validation cohort was available. PAX1 methylation was assessed as a prespecified exploratory single-marker comparator. In this selected sample, the combined model had a higher apparent AUC than the SOX1-only model (0.882 vs 0.828). At the Youden-derived threshold, sensitivity was 83.3 % and specificity was 88.3 %. Exploratory DCA favored the combined model within the study sample, but this estimate is dependent on the fixed case-control sampling fraction. The PAX1-only AUC methylation was 0.845, numerically higher than the SOX1-only AUC, although PAX1 was not included in multivariable modeling. Adding age and sex to the plasma SOX1 methylation signal improved apparent discrimination within this small selected cohort. This preliminary, hypothesis-generating model is not validated for clinical use and should not be assumed to generalize to consecutive hematuria populations. Independent prospective evaluation in larger, clinically representative cohorts is required.

records.title: Multi-omics in coronary atherosclerosis: mechanistic insights and advances in precision diagnosis and treatment.
records.abstract: Coronary atherosclerosis, driven by the interplay of lipid metabolic derangements and chronic inflammation, constitutes the pathological basis of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and has emerged as the leading cause of mortality among Chinese residents. In patients with acute coronary syndrome, subsequent events may arise from initially nonculprit coronary lesions that appear angiographically mild. Invasive coronary angiography, the conventional diagnostic reference standard, is inherently invasive and incapable of characterizing plaque biological properties. Meanwhile, traditional risk factors only enable crude risk stratification, resulting in a critical shortage of precise early clinical screening modalities. Multi-omics technologies enable comprehensive molecular profiling of the human organism and effectively address the limitations of conventional detection approaches. Nevertheless, existing investigations remain largely confined to single-omics analyses; candidate biomarkers lack validation in large independent cohorts, and substantial bottlenecks persist in clinical translation. This review evaluates the respective advantages and limitations of genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and gut metagenomics in coronary atherosclerosis research. It elucidates the scientific value of integrated multi-omics analysis in dissecting pathogenic regulatory networks, unraveling gut-heart axis mechanisms, and identifying targets for precision therapy. Furthermore, it summarizes cutting-edge technological advances including single-cell multi-omics, spatial multi-omics, liquid biopsy, and AI-powered multi-omics integration, and compiles multi-omics risk prediction models developed on the basis of large-scale population cohorts. By bridging genetic susceptibility, cellular remodeling, peripheral molecular signatures, and plaque phenotypes, multi-omics integration can underpin early risk warning for high-risk populations, plaque subtyping, and therapeutic efficacy monitoring. Looking ahead, the establishment of standardized, multicenter prospective cohorts and the application of Mendelian randomization to infer causal relationships will be pivotal. These efforts are essential to translate multi-omics into a practical framework for comprehensive precision medicine across the entire continuum of coronary atherosclerosis.

records.title: From liquid biopsy to spatial liquid biopsy: extracellular vesicles as molecular maps of cancer metastasis.
records.abstract: Cancer metastasis remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality, yet current liquid biopsy approaches provide limited information regarding the anatomical distribution of metastatic disease. Circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, and extracellular vesicle (EV)-based assays have substantially advanced molecular characterization of cancer but generally do not reveal the tissue sites where metastatic progression is occurring. Here, we introduce the concept of Spatial Liquid Biopsy, a proposed next-generation framework that utilizes circulating tumor-associated EVs as molecular maps of metastatic disease. We hypothesize that EVs released from metastatic lesions may carry both tumor-associated signatures and tissue-associated extracellular proteins reflecting interactions with the local metastatic microenvironment. By integrating tumor-associated EV enrichment with multiplex profiling of organ-associated surface markers, Spatial Liquid Biopsy seeks to identify composite tumor-associated/organ-associated EV signatures that may provide greater spatial specificity than either marker alone. If experimentally and clinically validated, these signatures may enable minimally invasive inference of metastatic organ involvement and longitudinal assessment of metastatic disease evolution. This framework represents a conceptual expansion of liquid biopsy from detecting circulating evidence of malignancy toward generating spatial information that may complement imaging and guide personalized cancer surveillance and management.

records.title: The Occurrence of Calcification in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma: Mechanism and Clinical Characteristics.
records.abstract: Calcification is a hallmark imaging feature of papillary thyroid carcinoma, present in 50% to 70% of cases and closely associated with tumor aggressiveness and prognosis. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the pathogenesis, imaging characteristics, molecular mechanisms, and clinical implications of calcification in papillary thyroid carcinoma. We discuss the formation of psammoma bodies (microcalcifications) and dystrophic calcifications, their correlation with BRAF V600E mutations and MAPK pathway activation, and their diagnostic and prognostic significance. Emerging evidence suggests calcification patterns can predict lymph node metastasis, recurrence risk, and response to therapy, guiding personalized management. Future directions include liquid biopsy for calcification-associated biomarkers and targeted therapies modulating mineralization pathways.
